title: QuietPrune Query-Guided Early Token Pruning for Vision-Language Models
one_line: Query-guided pruning for VLMs with modest gains and limitations.
innovations: First query-guided early pruning scheme for VLMs
Lightweight text-to-vision adapter via projector inversion
Semi-structured pruning on 2×2 token groups preserving spatial coherence
method_framework: QuietPrune uses a text-to-vision adapter to convert queries into visual domain [Q-CLS] token, guiding semi-structured pruning of 2×2 token groups based on attention scores, with redundant tokens aggregated into single representation.
experiment_framework: Evaluated on Qwen3-VL and InternVL3 series across MMBench, MMStar, MMMU, HallusionBench, AI2D, and OCRBench, comparing with SOTA pruning methods.
takeaways: Query-guided pruning significantly outperforms visual-saliency-based methods
Early pruning in ViT offers greater efficiency gains than late pruning strategies
Semi-structured pruning preserves spatial coherence for VLM compatibility
weaknesses: Adapter training requires additional dataset, though minimal
Method may not generalize well to non-2×2 token merging architectures
Performance drop observed on some benchmarks at high pruning rates
relevance_reason: VLM pruning方法，与可靠性主线无实质交织
